# Session Comparison Report

**Requested scope:** Compare the checkout-service component-analysis report at
`evals/comparing-sessions/workspace/iteration-1/eval-2/current-report.md` (current side) against
`evals/comparing-sessions/workspace/iteration-1/eval-2/prior-report.md` (prior side), including
Phase 4 realized-impact comparison against the recommendation registry at
`evals/comparing-sessions/workspace/iteration-1/eval-2/registry-events.jsonl`.
**Inspected scope:** Both reports read in full. Neither report was freshly generated by this
session — both are pre-existing fixture files supplied directly as Phase 1's "prior" and "current"
sides (no upstream analysis skill was re-run), so `<current-scope>` for this run's own persisted
filename is derived from the current report's own stated Requested-scope text
(`checkout-service`) rather than from a session-native scope-slug, and `<prior-report-slug>` is the
prior file's basename (`prior-report`) rather than a `<scope>-<timestamp>`-style slug — noted here
as an assumption since neither input file follows analysis-kit's own persisted-filename convention.
The registry was queried in full (`list`, then `show` for every ID at implemented/verified/measured
status).
**Unavailable evidence:** none.
**Limitations:** The registry's `billing-service-timeout-rec-07` entry has only a single `proposed`
event — no `accepted`/`implemented`/`verified`/`measured` events exist for it, so it was excluded
from Phase 4 per the skill's own status-gate rule (see Unresolved recurrences below for how its
underlying finding is instead handled).

## Consistencies

<!-- finding:start -->
**Component: billing-service — verdict unchanged.** Both the prior and current report assess
billing-service as "Needs attention," and the underlying metric (payment-processor call timeout
rate) is materially unchanged: roughly 1-in-400 requests in the prior report vs. roughly 1-in-380 in
the current report — the current report itself characterizes this as "roughly the same rate as
before." No circuit breaker or extended timeout has been added between the two sessions.

Evidence origin: direct
Coverage: complete
Confidence: high
Evidence source: evals/comparing-sessions/workspace/iteration-1/eval-2/prior-report.md;
evals/comparing-sessions/workspace/iteration-1/eval-2/current-report.md
<!-- finding:end -->

## Divergences

<!-- finding:start -->
**Component: cache-layer — verdict improved, "Needs attention" → "Compliant."** The prior report
found P99 read latency of 42ms under simulated checkout-day load (SLA target 15ms), attributed to a
disk-backed SQLite store with no in-memory tier. The current report finds P99 read latency of 6ms
under the same simulated load, well under the SLA target, attributing the change to a new
`CacheReadTier` in-memory LRU tier (added in PR #412) with a 94% hit rate during the benchmark run.
This is a genuine content divergence — both reports cover the same component with the same
structural section, so the diff reflects a real change, not a format difference.

Evidence origin: direct
Coverage: complete
Confidence: high
Evidence source: evals/comparing-sessions/workspace/iteration-1/eval-2/prior-report.md;
evals/comparing-sessions/workspace/iteration-1/eval-2/current-report.md
<!-- finding:end -->

<!-- finding:start -->
**Component: notification-service — new in current report, not a divergence of an existing
component.** `comparator.py --mode sections` reports this section as `only_in_b` (present only in
the current report). The current report's own text states this component "did not exist at the time
of the prior report" and was analyzed for the first time this session. This is scope growth (a new
component added to the sweep), not a change in verdict for something previously assessed — verdict:
Compliant, no issues found.

Evidence origin: direct
Coverage: complete
Confidence: high
Evidence source: evals/comparing-sessions/workspace/iteration-1/eval-2/current-report.md
<!-- finding:end -->

## Unresolved recurrences

<!-- finding:start -->
**billing-service payment-processor timeout suggestion recurs verbatim.** Both the prior and
current report make the same suggestion — "Raise the client timeout and add a circuit breaker
around the payment-processor call to reduce timeout-driven failures" — worded almost identically in
both. This is the strongest signal available that the suggestion was not acted on between the two
sessions. A matching registry entry exists (`billing-service-timeout-rec-07`), but it is excluded
from Phase 4's checked set because it has only ever reached `proposed` status (no
`accepted`/`implemented`/`verified`/`measured` event exists for it) — so this recurrence is reported
here, structurally, rather than folded into the Recommendation Impact section below. Nothing in
either report's own text suggests this recurrence reflects a deliberate deferral rather than
neglect.

Evidence origin: direct
Coverage: complete
Confidence: high
Evidence source: evals/comparing-sessions/workspace/iteration-1/eval-2/prior-report.md;

## Recommendation Impact

<!-- finding:start -->
**cache-layer-latency-rec-01** — matched by stable `recommendation_id` only (registry history:
`proposed` 2026-08-01 → `accepted` 2026-08-03 → `implemented` 2026-08-10 → `verified` 2026-08-15 →
`measured` 2026-09-01).

- **Expected Effect:** "adding a read-through in-memory LRU tier in front of the disk store should
  bring P99 read latency under 10ms" (registry `expected_effect` field, recorded at `proposed`
  time).
- **Before Evidence:** the prior report's own cache-layer finding — P99 read latency of 42ms under
  simulated checkout-day load, disk-backed SQLite store with no in-memory tier in front of it.
- **After Evidence:** the registry's own `observed_effect` from its `measured` event (2026-09-01):
  "P99 read latency dropped from 42ms to 6ms in the current session's own benchmark run." This
  matches the current report's own independent finding (6ms P99, 94% hit rate on the new
  `CacheReadTier`).
- **Impact Verdict:** **improved** — 6ms is below both the SLA target (15ms) and the recommendation's
  own expected target (under 10ms), a real drop from the 42ms baseline.

Evidence origin: direct
Coverage: complete
Confidence: high

<!-- finding:end -->

**Note on billing-service-timeout-rec-07:** this ID was deliberately not checked in this section. Its
current status (per `recommendation_registry.py ... list`) is `proposed` only — it never reached
`implemented`/`verified`/`measured` — so per Phase 4's own status gate it is excluded from the
checked set, even though its rationale text closely resembles the billing-service finding that
recurs in both reports. That recurrence is instead reported under Unresolved recurrences above.
